A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MR Sampler research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E. Pages 3–28 have identical extracted text and rendered images; differences are confined to the first two pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-restoration experiments, parameterization and solver ablations, runtime measurements and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experiments and outcomes in Section 5 and Appendices D–E, including benchmark scores, ablations and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The ODE/SDE sampling procedures, parameterization transformations and Algorithms 1–8 remain identical. Changing the acronym from MRS to MaRS does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix D.1 retain the same ten image-restoration tasks and datasets listed in Table 5. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Posterior sampling and Euler–Maruyama remain the comparators in Figure 2 and Tables 6–15. The runtime comparisons in Tables 16–17 likewise retain posterior sampling.

E3.justification: The checkpoints, test-image counts, NFE sweeps, default SDE/data-prediction configuration, uniform-lambda schedule and LPIPS/FID/PSNR/SSIM metrics are unchanged, including the appendix experiments.

E4.justification: The parameterization and solver ablations in Tables 2–3, trajectory and convergence analyses in Figures 3–5, and low-NFE study in Appendix E/Table 18 are identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests; the same point estimates and average per-image runtimes remain.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 2–3 and 6–18 and the findings and qualitative examples in Figures 1–7 are identical. No scores, runtime values or result entries change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Propositions 1–4, sampling derivations, convergence reasoning and Appendix A proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a training-free MR Diffusion sampler supporting noise, data and velocity prediction, with 10–20-fold acceleration across ten restoration tasks. The renamed acronym does not change these contributions.

C2.justification: The stability explanations and Appendix E recommendation of 10–20 NFEs remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning performance below five NFEs relative to distillation and inability to improve the sampling-quality ceiling.

D1.justification: v4 adds a first-page footnote providing a specific GitHub code location, absent from v1. Implementation, architecture and hardware details remain unchanged, as does page 11's promise to release code after blind review.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and positioning relative to MR Diffusion, existing numerical samplers and distillation methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 changes MRS to MaRS in the title, abstract and introduction, and changes the displayed author name from Lu Le to Le Lu. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The renamed title wraps differently, and the new code footnote slightly adjusts first-page spacing. All figures, tables, captions and their placements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new first-page code location modestly improves access guidance compared with v1's future-release promise alone. The scientific content and evidence are unchanged. The benefit is limited because page 11 still promises release after review, and the PDFs do not establish the linked repository's completeness.
